hero.title: Religion in the Sangam Age
hero.description: An analytical exploration of the polytheistic, animistic, and nascent Vedic traditions characterizing the Sangam period (300 BCE – 300 CE).

timeline.title: The Chronological Framework
timeline.description: Phases of religious evolution in Southern India.

cards.details: Predominance of indigenous animism and worship of local deities like Murugan.
Increased Aryanization; assimilation of Vedic rituals and Brahmanical influence alongside traditional cults.

items.title: T.I.N.A
items.decryption: Remember that Sangam religion was rooted in the 5 Thinais (ecological zones) with indigenous, non-Vedic animistic foundations.

traps.title: UPSC Common Exam Traps
items: Assuming the Sangam period was purely Vedic; it was actually a blend of tribal folk religion and emerging Brahmanism.
Confusing 'Hero Stone' (Viragal) worship with Buddhist Stupa worship; Hero stones are indigenous Tamil traditions.
Thinking temples existed in the 'stone-structure' sense; early places of worship were 'Manrams' or open-air sacred groves.

sections.title: 1. Core Study Notes
sections.content:
Geography (Thinais)

  • Kurinji: Murugan (Hills)
  • Mullai: Mayon/Vishnu (Forests)
  • Marutam: Indiran (Agriculture)
  • Neital: Varunan (Coastal)
  • Palai: Kotravai/Durga (Desert)

Religious Elements

  • Hero Stone (Viragal)
  • Animism & Totemism
  • Ancestor Worship
  • Asceticism (Samanar/Buddhist)
  • Indigenous Core:
    • Murugan as the supreme deity (Seyon).
    • Hero stone worship (Viragal) to commemorate fallen warriors.
    • Totemism and nature spirits.
  • Vedic Integration:
    • Introduction of Yagnas by Brahmins.
    • Gods like Vishnu, Shiva, and Balarama adopted.
  • Ascetic Traditions:
    • Rise of Buddhism and Jainism (Samanar).
    • Influence of wandering monks on Sangam society.
